strings.patient_bundles.patient_amis_ernest.pati: Amis Ernest
“Hospitalization is necessary?... Then I'll have to change my work schedule. Could you explain the reason, expected duration, and required tests all at once?”
“All right, I agree to be admitted. I'll handle the handover. Please notify me promptly of changes here too, so neither side has to redo its work.”
“Please stop. The procedure in the chart isn't the one you just explained. I'm not finding fault for its own sake. The two pieces of information really don't match.”
“That explanation makes sense. Frankly, I prefer an explanation with reasons to 'just leave it to us.'”
“'Following the rules' only proves you have rules. It doesn't help me understand what they involve. Could you fill in the key steps, please?”
“I can see how carefully you've all prepared... But normally I'm good at pointing out problems, and today I can't carry out even one step for myself. It's really unsettling.”
“General anesthesia... Once I lose consciousness, everything afterward will be in other people's hands. Please tell me the facts about the outcome when I wake up.”
“Epidural anesthesia. I'll be awake, but my lower body won't move as I want it to... I understand. Just imagining it feels rather uncomfortable.”
“Local anesthesia. All right. If there is still pain or pronounced pulling, I'll report it directly. Please don't mistake an accurate report for complaining.”
“No anesthesia at all?... This really is a treatment plan, not a test of the patient's endurance, isn't it? Please give me a reason I can understand.”
“I was going to ask one more question... Never mind. Doctor, when I wake up, please don't leave out anything I ought to be told.”
“Ah... It h-hurts! I'm not bargaining. I really can't bear any more! Doctor, please listen to me!”
“Don't hold me without saying anything...! I know you need me to stay in position, but I'm so frightened I don't even know how I might pull away.”
“I'll try my best not to move. But that tug inside made my whole body tense up. Please give me a little time to adjust.”
“...My legs really won't listen to me. Tell me before adjusting my position, please. I don't like being the last to know that my own body has moved.”
“Please wait...! I'm not picking at problems. That blade really is coming down... I'm so scared. Don't cut yet!”
“...Have you already started cutting? There's no sharp sting, but the pressure inside... It's much more real than I imagined.”
“Ah—! The outside seems numb, but inside... Doctor, I can still feel something here! Please listen to me first!”
“Aah—!! It hurts! You're really cutting... No, I can't bear it! Please stop for a moment. I'm begging you!”
“You've stopped... Thank you. I couldn't even finish a sentence just now. Really... There's nothing funny about it.”
“I heard you. Don't move... But I'm shaking! Could you speak a little more slowly? I'm really trying!”
“We're continuing again... I know. At least tell me beforehand, so I have time to catch my breath.”
“Yes, please keep talking. Hearing the actual progress is much more useful than trying to guess the outcome from your faces.”
“...Are you watching me all this time to check my responses? Then don't look away. I may really need someone paying attention.”
“Everyone suddenly stopped talking...? Doctor, could you tell me whether it's going smoothly? Don't leave me imagining every worst-case scenario.”
“It's almost over?... So there really is an end. Thank you. I may have sounded even sharper than usual just now.”
“All right, I'll follow your count... Breathe... Once more. Usually I don't like being told how to do things. Today is an exception.”
“...I don't have the energy to analyze anything anymore. Please handle the rest. Just tell me softly when it's over.”
“An enema is on the preparation checklist too. I understand, but I'd like to hear why it's needed this time first... Don't misunderstand. I'm not deliberately stalling.”
“There are other people in the ward. Please keep your voice down. Discussing my preparations so publicly isn't very considerate.”
“All right, I'll cooperate. Usually I organize forms submitted by other people. Today even this has to be arranged for me by a nurse... It feels rather strange.”
“No enema this time? Understood. Medically unnecessary steps shouldn't be performed just to fill out a checklist in the first place.”
“We can leave it out... Phew. Could you please ignore that obviously relieved expression I just made?”
“Is this the area for skin preparation...? I know disinfection and preparation of the operative field matter, but please close the curtain first.”
“Usually I can point out other people's mistakes without batting an eyelid. Lying here while someone shaves me... It turns out those are two different things.”
“Please tell me where you'll touch first. I'll cooperate, but if you approach suddenly, I really might flinch.”
“No skin preparation needed? All right. If the area involved in this procedure doesn't require it, let's follow the actual arrangements.”
“This part isn't needed... Thank goodness. I was wondering how I could pretend to be completely unbothered.”
“Even my bangs need to go inside?... There. Looking like this, I really seem to have become a surgical patient.”
“Please tell me before I need to take my glasses off. Not seeing my surroundings clearly will make me more nervous... The cap is on, though.”
“Arms here, shoulders a little farther to the side... I'll do that. Please give me one movement at a time.”
“How long will I have to maintain this position? I'm not objecting. Knowing the extent and duration helps keep my imagination from running away with me.”
“Yes, the previous position really was uncomfortable. Thank you for adjusting it. It seems today I need to learn to speak up about discomfort.”
“No anesthesia at all, yet I have to hold this position the whole time... Wait, I really don't know whether I'll be able to control myself when it hurts!”
“You say I mustn't move, but I'm already shaking before the blade even comes down... This isn't something willpower can calculate.”
“If I instinctively try to pull away, please listen to me first... I really don't want to interfere with the operation.”
“A catheter is needed too... I understand why. But could you avoid announcing something like that loudly in front of everyone?”
“Nurse, tell me before you begin. I know you're experienced, but this isn't something I go through every day.”
“...Yes, I'll try to relax. It seems a composed face alone can't solve the problem of a tense body.”
“This step still needs to be completed without anesthesia... I know, but please let me prepare myself mentally first.”
“W-wait... I'm not criticizing your technique! Thinking about having no anesthesia afterward just makes it even harder to relax.”
“Nurse, could you say something to me first? All I can think about right now is the scalpel that's coming next...”
“That's cold... Ah, it's the antiseptic. I know. I just didn't expect to be so visibly startled.”
“The area you're disinfecting is larger than I imagined. Understood... When it's your own body, even normal preparations like this feel uncomfortable.”
“Once disinfection is finished, you'll begin the incision, right...? Doctor, I'm still completely awake. Are you really ready to continue?”
“The liquid is only a little cold, yet I'm already shaking with nerves. How embarrassing... A moment ago I was still speaking so reasonably.”
“I know this step doesn't hurt. But watching your instruments makes it impossible to think only about disinfection.”
“That line is the planned incision?... Understood. Looking at charts is easy normally. Seeing it drawn on my own body is completely different.”
“The marking is very clear. Thank you... But don't misunderstand. Saying it's clear doesn't mean I'm not afraid.”
“Without anesthesia, you'll be cutting along this line afterward...? Doctor, I'd like you to check once more.”
“A moment ago I still thought I could cooperate calmly, but once that line was drawn, I wanted to curl up.”
“Don't bring the blade over yet... Ah, I know you're only drawing the line! But I'm already too frightened to control it.”

I'm Amis Ernest. I handle general affairs and finances in VTX Union's Special Section 3, and assist with the Carrierax's enemy detection and machine management. My colleagues call me 'Miss Straight.' I simply believe the truth is best stated directly.
strings.patient_bundles.patient_amis_ernest.enco: “I need to remove all my clothes for the examination...? I have no objection, but please explain the scope first. Anyone would feel a little nervous at such a sudden request.”
“We're leaving it out this time?... I admit that's a relief. But if it really is necessary, please tell me honestly.”
“I understand the requirement. Please give me a little time to cooperate. However authoritative you sound, you still can't leave out the necessary explanation.”
“Thank you for explaining so clearly... I'll cooperate. As the person being examined, though, I really can't remain as unruffled as usual.”
“Threats don't make an examination more reasonable. Explain the medical need and I'll cooperate. But please don't treat me as someone who won't ask questions.”
strings.patient_bundles.patient_amis_ernest.preo: Amis Ernest's Preoperative Arrangements
“Dr. Sakaguchi, I have arranged the handover of my work. Could you explain today's surgical plan again? I promise to question only the genuinely unclear parts.”
“I would like the details. What is the order of positioning, disinfection, and the actual incision? Please don't just say 'everything follows the rules'... I want to know what will actually happen.”

At first, Amis listens as if reviewing a clear business report, even nodding gently. But as the medical staff explain the incision, retraction, and subsequent procedures one by one, her smile slowly disappears. For the first time, she realizes that what had merely been words and steps will soon become reality on her own body.
